newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Globalstar sees big satellite phone system market.
newsitem.headline: Globalstar sees big satellite phone system market.

text.p: U.S.-based Globalstar expects to capture a wide market of cellular phone users for its new satellite phone system when its global network is set up in 1999, a senior official said on Tuesday.

"We are positioned to capture both markets, those who are currently using cellular phones and those who need wider satellite coverage," Ming Louie, Asia Pacific vice president for Business Development said at a press conference.
Globalstar will launch its first satellites in the third quarter this year and 40 satellites should be ready at the end of 1998.

The full constellation of 48 satellites is scheduled for completion in the first half of 1999 and will provide wireless telephone services to all areas of the world where Globalstar is authorised to operate, Louie said.
He said the hand-held satellite telephone was heavier than existing cellular versions, but would complement their use as worldwide connections would be more expansive.

About 50 percent of sales were likely to come from the dual phone market, where it is compatible with virtually all current and future mobile and switched telephone networks -- Global System for Mobile (GSM) and Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA), he said.
Globalstar aimed to get the other 50 percent from remote areas where there are no fixed systems or telephone lines.
It expected to see positive cash flow by 1999, soon after it launches full global service, Louie said.
He said 1999 was the more aggressive target but the plan was to have some three million customers by 2002.
The company has raised US$2 billion out of the US$2.5 billion forecast for the cost of the project and could return to the market to raise the remaining US$500 million, Louie said.
"The current challenge is that we are approved in the regulatory markets, obtaining local licences to operate," he said.
